_meta.source: main page ('our insights': the future of intelligence is distributed; vision); research/harness_bodies_death (swarms, hierarchies)

failure_modes: Model style convergence: instances too similar to hold different information
Exchanges without selection flood each instance with noise
A hub instance quietly becomes a central controller

Unstructured swarm: with no orchestration, internal bureaucracy grows and the swarm slowly reinvents the structure it could have been given; light structure such as {{coordinator_lane_topology}} is far more efficient
gloss: Many model instances selectively exchange information to reduce uncertainty about their environments
invariants: Each instance acts on local information plus what others choose to share
No single instance holds or controls the collective model
mechanism: Different instantiations of similar models, each updating by a {{local_learning_rule}}, selectively exchange and interpret each other's information to reduce uncertainty about their environments, each practising {{prediction_error_minimization}}. No instance holds the whole picture. The collective capability is an instance of {{self_organisation}}: it arises from the exchanges and is not specified by any one instance.
